hooks.text: A rescue train planned for 250 children never left Prague.
Why did the planned 250-child rescue train never leave Prague?

title: The Winton Rescue Train That Never Left Prague
description: Nicholas Winton and his team helped 669 children reach Britain, but their planned transport for 250 children was cancelled on 1 September 1939 as Germany invaded Poland. Winton’s scrapbook helped bring the rescue story to public attention in 1988. Visual context: Winton portrait, 1938; Prague Main Station aerial, 1931, labeled as a location view; Winton memorial at Prague station, photographed in 2015. No scene depicts the cancelled train or its children.
